summary: A course companion for choosing between Craig Jones’s half-guard, headlock-response and turtle material in Octopus Guard 2.0.
description: Locate a recurring no-gi bottom-position problem in the published Octopus Guard 2.0 syllabus.
overview: The title covers more than one guard position: the outline moves from half guard and side control to headlock responses and turtle. Choose the section that matches your problem before treating the course as a single attack sequence.

fits: You want to investigate no-gi half-guard exchanges that lead into headlock or turtle situations.
consider_alternative_if: For gi sleeve entries and a compact sweep/back-take survey, compare Eduardo Telles’s Octopus With Pajamas.

includes: Half-guard versus side-control distinctions and crossface discussion in volume 1.
Sweeping and D’Arce-related responses in volume 2; headlock and turtle branches continue in volumes 3–4.
limits: This no-gi release extends into headlock responses, buggy-choke material and turtle; it is broader than a compact sweep-and-back-take introduction.
It does not offer the gi sleeve-entry emphasis of Telles’s Octopus With Pajamas.

start_here.title: Locate your first lost position
start_here.task: Compare volume 1’s half-guard/side-control discussion with the later headlock and turtle headings. In a bottom-position exchange you can review, record whether the problem begins while a leg is still trapped or after a side pin is established. If you own the course, start with the half-guard comparison and check the instructor’s distinction before choosing a counter section.
